headline: Phillies riding six-game streak into Cardinals opener
recap: The Phillies were off Thursday, still riding the six-game winning streak they built by sweeping the Marlins at home. The finale came Wednesday, when Aaron Nola struck out eight over seven innings and Luis Arraez homered and drove in two as Philadelphia beat Miami 4-1. The Phillies scored in the second, third and seventh innings off Sandy Alcantara and reliever John King; Javier Sanoja's solo home run in the sixth was the only run against Nola, who improved to 5-9. Trea Turner and Garrett Stubbs each added an RBI, and Jhoan Duran closed it out for his 28th save.
Philadelphia is 70-58, in second place in the NL East, five games behind the first-place Braves (75-53).

The Phillies open a three-game series at home against the Cardinals on Friday night, with Jesus Luzardo on the mound; St. Louis has not yet announced a starter. First pitch is scheduled for 6:40 PM ET, with Philadelphia a -206 moneyline favorite.
